classification.difficultyReason: Apply the inscribed-angle theorem to equal peg intervals, then reverse it to establish the least possible peg count.

children.label: a
children.prompt: A circular pegboard has twelve equally spaced pegs placed around its circumference. A triangle is drawn using three of the pegs as vertices, as shown below. Find the three angles in the triangle.

spec.description: Twelve equally spaced black circumference pegs, with triangle vertices at the top, leftmost and lower-right pegs. Source cyan fill is omitted; all three triangle sides are explicit.
spec.mathematics: Clockwise from the top vertex, the triangle arcs span four, five and three intervals of 30 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: No angle values, arc counts or vertex names are printed.

answer.worked:
Each interval between adjacent pegs subtends a central angle of
$$\frac{360^\circ}{12}=30^\circ.$$
Each triangle angle is half the central angle spanning its opposite arc. The opposite arcs contain five, four and three peg intervals respectively:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Top angle}&=\tfrac12\times5\times30^\circ\\\text{Top angle}&=75^\circ\\\text{Left angle}&=\tfrac12\times4\times30^\circ\\\text{Left angle}&=60^\circ\\\text{Lower-right angle}&=\tfrac12\times3\times30^\circ\\\text{Lower-right angle}&=45^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Another pegboard also has equally spaced pegs. A triangle is drawn using three of the pegs as vertices. Given the triangle has angles $50^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $70^\circ$, find the least possible number of pegs on the board.

answer.short:
$18$ pegs.

The opposite arcs subtend $100^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $140^\circ$ at the centre; their greatest common divisor is $20^\circ$.
answer.worked:
By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, the three opposite arcs subtend central angles of $100^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $140^\circ$.

With $n$ equally spaced pegs, adjacent pegs subtend $\frac{360^\circ}{n}$. Each of the three arcs must contain a whole number of these intervals. The least peg count uses the greatest possible interval angle, the greatest common divisor of $100^\circ$, $120^\circ$ and $140^\circ$, which is $20^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{360^\circ}{n}&=20^\circ\\n&=\frac{360}{20}\\n&=18\end{align*}$$
This is possible because the three arcs contain $5$, $6$ and $7$ intervals, totalling $18$. Therefore, the least possible number is $18$ pegs.
